transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-07-23
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Jamie Carter (Redwood AE); Priya Singh (Redwood SE); Luis Moreno (Redwood CSM); Elliot Park (Argonaut Head of ML); Maya Chen (Argonaut Platform Eng); Rafael Ortiz (Argonaut Product Lead); Sasha Iqbal (Argonaut Security)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, optional):
- Review of latest scorecard metrics, small regression on named-entity extraction after prompt pruning; discussed lowering scoring threshold, guardrail tuning, and running targeted regression sweeps.
- Action items: SE to run regression sweep, CSM to set up dedicated-node benchmark, Redwood to share security docs.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jamie Carter: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you making the time. Quick roll call — I see Elliot, Maya, Rafael, Sasha — hi — and from our side Priya and Luis. We're on for 55 minutes, main goals are the weekly check-in, go over the scorecard, any regressions, and agree on next steps.

[00:25] Elliot Park: Yep thanks Jamie. We mostly want to get clarity on a couple of surprising FP spikes in the last 48 hours. We had three high-confidence false positives in entity normalization which is odd because our baseline looked cleaner last week.

[00:40] Priya Singh: Yeah I pulled the heatmap — there is a cluster around mid-length prompts where the embedding similarity threshold seems to be off after we pruned a few system instructions. Could be prompt drift or the short-circuiting we did for the prefix cache.

[01:05] Maya Chen: Just to clarify, when you say prefix cache, you mean the KV cache on the runner, right, the kay vee cache?

[01:10] Priya Singh: Right sorry, the KV cache. There's also a chance the new prompt ordering triggers a different attention pattern so the model weights aren't being, uh, used exactly the same. We saw a slight change in token alignments.

[01:30] Rafael Ortiz: From product we rolled a prompt pruning change to reduce token cost. The aim was to cut 8-10% off token usage. We expected some trade-offs but the regression isn't huge, just one class of entity that's mis-normalized to a company name.

[01:50] Luis Moreno: Quick question on observability — are those failure cases concentrated by user segment or random?

[02:00] Elliot Park: Mostly enterprise accounts using longer multi-field forms, yes. That's why it's higher priority.

[02:18] Priya Singh: Ok, so plan: I recommend lowering the scoring acceptance threshold from 0.72 to 0.68 for the model variant we're running under the hosted config and re-run the evaluation on the recent 2k examples. Also we should add an extra guardrail: a post-processing check that rejects entity normalizations when confidence is low and falls back to a strict regex or DB lookup.

[02:45] Sasha Iqbal: From security perspective we need to make sure any fallback to DB lookup does not leak PII. We'll need explicit audit logging and a note in the data flow doc about transient encryption keys. Also remind — do you support HSM-backed KMS for private deployments?

[03:05] Jamie Carter: Yes, for Redwood Private we integrate with customer KMS/HSM — we have certed integrations. I'll send the security pack including SOC2 type II artifacts and KMS docs after the call.

[03:20] Sasha Iqbal: Great, please include SSO/SAML details and RBAC defaults. Also retention on logs — we need to know what gets stored and for how long.

[03:35] Jamie Carter: We'll include that. Luis, do we have a link to the security page we can share?

[03:40] Luis Moreno: Yep I'll drop the links in the follow-up and attach the latest SOC2 attestation PDF.

[03:48] Priya Singh: Back to the scorecard: I ran a quick split by prompt length. Short prompts under 40 tokens are fine; long prompts above 240 tokens are fine. It's the mid band 80–180 tokens where the subtle change caused boundary condition errors — likely because the context window interacts with our truncation heuristics.

[04:15] Rafael Ortiz: Are we confident this is model-decoding behavior and not an artifact of tokenization differences between the variants?

[04:22] Priya Singh: Good call — tokenization differences can sneak in. I checked the tokenizer hashes, they match across the runs, so it's not that. More likely it's the prompt rewrite we applied which removed a clarifying clause in some cases.

[04:40] Elliot Park: If the prompt rewrite saved us 9% token cost but introduced these FPs, we need a cost vs quality decision. How much does this impact our key metric — conversion rate on enterprise form completion?

[04:55] Rafael Ortiz: We estimate a 0.8% hit on conversion in impacted flows. Not catastrophic but noticeable for some deals.

[05:10] Priya Singh: Option A: revert rewrite for enterprise segment only — can do as a routing rule. Option B: keep rewrite and add the stricter postprocessing fallback for enterprise. Option C: move enterprise to a dedicated capacity run with slightly different quantization/profile to reduce variance.

[05:35] Maya Chen: Can you say more about dedicated vs hosted differences here? We've been on hosted, but we are evaluating Dedicated because of predictable latency.

[05:45] Jamie Carter: Sure — hosted gives you fast onboarding and autoscaled pools; Dedicated reserves GPU capacity for your workloads which reduces noisy neighbor variance and lets you pick quantization profiles and kernel selections. For a subtle regression like this, Dedicated can remove some sources of variance, but it's not always the root cause.

[06:10] Priya Singh: Also with Dedicated we can pin model variants and do canary rollouts per tenant. That would let you revert the prompt rewrite for enterprise accounts instantly while keeping it for smaller accounts.

[06:25] Elliot Park: That sounds promising. What's the timeline to spin up a dedicated node for a pilot?

[06:30] Luis Moreno: Typically 2–3 weeks for provisioning and baseline benchmarking if you sign the reserved capacity commitment; we can also do a short-term dedicated pilot in our hosted fleet to emulate the environment faster.

[06:45] Rafael Ortiz: For now, let's try the routing rule first and see if that fixes the conversion number. If not, we'll escalate to Dedicated.

[06:55] Priya Singh: Agreed. I'll scope the routing rule — it will check user segment and route to the 'enterprise-prompt-v1' variant which keeps the clarifying clause.

[07:10] Elliot Park: On scoring and eval — can we look at the scoring spreadsheet? The table shows precision dropped from 0.91 to 0.84 in that entity class.

[07:20] Priya Singh: Right. I did a confusion matrix — most errors are label-swaps, not blank misses. So guardrails that enforce canonicalization and an allowlist should catch many.

[07:36] Maya Chen: What about embeddings drift? We recently updated our DB of canonical entities; could mismatches cause the similarity scoring to decay?

[07:45] Priya Singh: Could be. I asked for the embedding anchors you folks are using — if those changed we need to re-run a small remap job. Maya, can you share the current anchor set?

[07:55] Maya Chen: Yes I'll export and send it. Also I'll include sample traffic distributions — percent long vs mid vs short prompts.

[08:05] Priya Singh: Great. Actionable next step there is I will re-run the regression sweep on the 2k recent examples with threshold 0.68 and produce the top 20 failures for you to review. That should tell us whether it's prompt rewrite or anchor mismatch.

[08:20] Elliot Park: Sounds good. Also if we identify a systemic embedding shift, what's the easiest way to remediate? Re-embed our canonical DB?

[08:30] Priya Singh: Yes re-embed anchors + rollout new embedding indices. Redwood supports phased rollouts so you can test on a subset first.

[08:40] Rafael Ortiz: On metrics — can we get a delta view on cost per 1k tokens and latency before and after the rewrite?

[08:45] Luis Moreno: I'll build a small dashboard with cost per 1k tokens, median and p95 latency, and a scorecard delta. I'll include both hosted and the simulated dedicated baseline.

[09:00] Jamie Carter: One thing to flag — if you end up wanting lower variance and full isolation, Dedicated has an upfront monthly commit. We'll include pricing options in the follow-up.

[09:10] Maya Chen: Okay. A security note — the Argonaut compliance team wants to validate data residency. We're in the EU region; any retention of logs in US regions would need to be disabled. Is that feasible?

[09:22] Luis Moreno: Yes, we can constrain region placement for Redwood Private and Dedicated; hosted instances have regional controls as well — we can show the options in the security docs.

[09:35] Sasha Iqbal: Please include the audit log retention defaults and whether you can redact query contents from logs for compliance.

[09:45] Jamie Carter: We'll include that.

[09:50] Priya Singh: Quick clarification on the scoring threshold — lowering from 0.72 to 0.68 will increase recall but may slightly lower precision. Given your conversion metric, Elliot, doing the sweep first is the safe step. If the failures are mostly canonicalization, we'll push the post-processing fallback.

[10:10] Elliot Park: Makes sense. Any concerns about latency with fallback? If we add a DB lookup fallback for enterprise, would that add significant tail latency?

[10:20] Priya Singh: It can add a small tail increase, but we can do the DB lookup asynchronously for non-blocking flows or cache the canonical DB in-memory for sub-10ms response. Dedicated gives you the headroom to do that without cost surprises.

[10:40] Rafael Ortiz: For the regression sweep, can you also flag whether the errors are deterministic given the same seed or stochastic? We want to know if reruns produce the same mis-normalization.

[10:50] Priya Singh: I'll include determinism checks in the sweep — re-run the top 100 cases three times.

[11:00] Luis Moreno: Quick housekeeping — I'll open a pilot tracking ticket in our shared project workspace and attach the scoring spreadsheet and the dataset used for the sweep.

[11:10] Jamie Carter: Perfect. Let's go through explicit next steps and owners now.

[11:15] Priya Singh: Action 1: Run regression sweep with threshold 0.68, produce top 20 failures and determinism results. Owner: Priya. Due 2025-07-28.

[11:25] Luis Moreno: Action 2: Create pilot dashboard with cost/latency/score deltas, include hosted vs dedicated simulation. Owner: Luis. Due 2025-07-30.

[11:35] Maya Chen: Action 3: Export and share canonical embedding anchor set + traffic distribution. Owner: Maya. Due 2025-07-25.

[11:45] Jamie Carter: Action 4: Send security pack (SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS/HSM integration notes, retention particulars). Owner: Jamie. Due 2025-07-25.

[11:55] Rafael Ortiz: One small ask — include a sample config for routing rule we discussed so our infra team can evaluate.

[12:05] Priya Singh: I'll draft the routing rule snippet and include it with the sweep results.

[12:15] Elliot Park: Ok thanks all. If the sweep shows it's prompt rewrite, we'll try the routing rule and hopefully avoid dedicated spend. If not, we'll discuss Dedicated pilot.

[12:30] Jamie Carter: Great. We'll follow up with the docs and the sweep results. Any final questions?

[12:38] Sasha Iqbal: No questions from security beyond what we covered.

[12:42] Maya Chen: Nothing else.

[12:45] Jamie Carter: Thanks everyone — we'll send notes and the links. Meeting adjourned.

References / links mentioned (to be included in follow-up):
- scorecard spreadsheet link (placeholder)
- security pack (SOC2, KMS/HSM, SSO) link
- pilot tracking ticket link

Meeting end.
